INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper. options.C: She sits more upright on the bicycle.
options.D: She starts to travel downhill.

An air bubble in a tank of water is rising with terminal (constant) velocity. The forces acting on the bubble are X, Y and Z, as shown. X velocity air bubble Y Z The upthrust on the bubble is X. Which statement about the forces is correct?

options.A: Z is the viscous force on the bubble, Y is the weight of the bubble and X = Y + Z.
options.B: Z is the viscous force on the bubble, Y is the weight of the bubble and X > Y + Z.
options.C: Z is the weight of the bubble, Y is the viscous force on the bubble and X = Y + Z.

options.A: Both blocks must travel with the same speed.
options.B: The steel block must travel faster than the wooden block.
options.C: The wooden block must travel faster than the steel block.
options.D: The masses of the blocks and the steel ball are needed to determine which block travels faster.

A solid wooden cube rests on a horizontal surface. What gives the pressure exerted by the weight of the cube on the horizontal surface?

questions.questionText: A bungee jumper jumps from a platform and is decelerated by an elastic bungee cord, as shown. platform bungee jumper bungee cord bungee cord ground ground NOT TO before jumping SCALE during the jump When the jumper makes the jump, his initial gravitational potential energy is converted into his kinetic energy and into elastic potential energy in the cord. questions.questionText: An object is displaced horizontally to the right in a uniform vertical gravitational field. Which statement describes the change in the gravitational potential energy of the object?

options.A: It decreases in direct proportion to the displacement.
options.B: It does not change with the displacement.
options.C: It increases in direct proportion to the displacement.
options.D: It increases in direct proportion to the square of the displacement.

An observer is standing on a railway platform. A train passes the observer at constant speed while emitting sound of constant frequency f from its whistle. What does the observer hear?

options.A: sound of a decreasing frequency as the train approaches and of an increasing frequency as it moves away
options.B: sound of a higher frequency than f as the train approaches and of a lower frequency than f as the train moves away

options.D: sound of an increasing frequency as the train approaches and as it moves away

options.C: fungi of length 50m

options.C: The waves travel in opposite directions.
options.D: The waves travel in the same direction.

questions.questionText: In an experiment to produce a stationary sound wave in air, a fine powder is initially evenly distributed along the length of a horizontal glass tube which is closed at one end. At the open end of the tube, a loudspeaker emits a sound wave of a constant wavelength. A stationary wave is formed and the powder accumulates in regularly spaced piles, as shown. glass tube loudspeaker piles of fine powder Which statement explains the positions of the piles of powder within the tube?

options.A: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate with maximum amplitude.
options.B: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate with minimum amplitude.
options.C: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate with the highest frequency.
options.D: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate vertically.

options.A: Double the amplitude of the sound wave.
options.B: Double the width of the doorway.
options.C: Halve the frequency of the sound wave.
options.D: Halve the period of the sound wave.
